questions.stem: Which structure is found in plant cells but NOT in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts are found only in plant cells (specifically in green parts) and are the site of photosynthesis. Both cell types have mitochondria, cell membranes, and ribosomes.

questions.stem: What is the plant cell wall made of?
questions.explanation: The plant cell wall is made primarily of cellulose, a complex carbohydrate that provides structural support and rigidity.

questions.stem: What is the membrane surrounding the vacuole called?
questions.explanation: The tonoplast is the membrane that surrounds the permanent vacuole in plant cells. The vacuole contains cell sap.

questions.stem: A plant cell that is firm due to water pressure is described as being:
questions.explanation: A turgid cell is one that is firm because the vacuole is full of water, pushing the cytoplasm against the cell wall and creating turgor pressure.

questions.stem: Why do plant cells have chloroplasts but animal cells do not?

options.text: Animal cells are too small for chloroplasts
Plants are autotrophs that make their own food through photosynthesis
Animal cells use chloroplasts for a different purpose
Chloroplasts only work in cells with a cell wall

questions.explanation: Plants are autotrophs and need chloroplasts to carry out photosynthesis to make their own food. Animals are heterotrophs that obtain food by eating other organisms.

questions.stem: Which statement about plant cells is a common misconception?

options.text: Plant cells have a cell wall outside the cell membrane
Plant cells have both mitochondria and chloroplasts

questions.explanation: Not all plant cells have chloroplasts. Only cells in the green parts of the plant (mainly leaves) have chloroplasts. Root cells, for example, do not contain chloroplasts.

questions.stem: What happens to a plant cell when it loses water?

options.text: The vacuole shrinks and the cell becomes flaccid

questions.explanation: When a plant cell loses water, the vacuole shrinks, turgor pressure is lost, and the cell becomes flaccid (soft). This causes the plant to wilt.
